name: Warm Longarm
description: Walk the throwing beam from butt to tip and test each lashing and iron band by hand before the crew mans the engine.

name: Even Slingpouch
description: Turn the winch crank to an even count with the crew so the beam descends smoothly without jerking the cable.

name: Steady Ballast
description: Lay the sling flat along the trough with the pouch at the foot and the free loop set over the release pin.

name: Judging Fulcrum
description: Lift the dressed shot with a straight back and roll it into the sling pouch without scraping the trough edge.

name: Swingdodge
description: On the warning call step back from the beam's arc and stand clear of swinging cable and falling gear.

name: Pulleydrop
description: Draw the trip lanyard with one short firm pull so the pin slips and the beam hurls the shot.

name: Armcount
description: Space each puller along the haul rope an arm's width apart so no two bodies crowd the same stretch of cable.

name: Gentle Releasehook
description: Pull the beam butt down on the count with the whole team leaning back together and heels dug in.

name: Smooth Shortarm
description: Dig both heels into packed earth and lock the knees so a sudden rope surge cannot drag the puller forward.

name: Judging Hangcradle
description: Gather the loose haul rope in even coils after the throw so it lies clear of the next team's feet.

name: Nimble Swing
description: Open every hand together on the release call and step aside as the rope whips through the sheave.

name: Rigging Count
description: Squat beside the dressed shot and lift it to the hip with a flat back and a locked grip.

name: Tending Tackle
description: Carry a heavy shot slung on a pole between two crewmen in matched step across the engine yard.

name: Mild Pullrope
description: Count and weigh the stacked shot by eye and by lift so the crew knows how many of each size are ready.

name: Pulleycount
description: Seat the shot deep in the sling pouch with both palms so it cannot roll when the sling snaps taut.

name: Tacklecount
description: Roll the shot up a short timber ramp to the trough lip with the whole crew pushing on one count.

name: Holding Shortarm
description: Plant a foot and a flat hand against a shot slipping from the ramp and bring it to rest before it runs on.

name: Warm Fulcrum
description: Breathe out fully at the top of each lift and drop the shoulders so the lifter tires slowly across a long day.

name: Pulleyreview
description: Wipe the release pin and its iron socket with tallow so it slides free at the pull and never sticks.

name: Judging Longarm
description: Study the pin tip for burrs and bent edges and set aside any pin that would snag the sling ring.

name: Watching Pullrope
description: Hook the sling ring onto the pin hook with a smooth flick of the wrist and a downward seat.

name: Armreview
description: Hold the trip line taut but not drawn through a long wait so the pin stays set until the order.

name: Sharp Counterswing
description: Snap the trip line back across the hip in one clean pull that frees the pin and throws the shot.

name: Pulleygauge
description: After the shot check that the pin fell clear and the hook is unbent before the arm is cranked down again.

name: Armnote
description: Lay a long board across the sill and read its balance by eye until both ends sit true on the ground.

name: Pulleynote
description: Raise each upright post and hold it plumb by hand while the crew drives the wedges that fix it.

name: Steady Hangcradle
description: Slide hardwood shims under the axle seat until the beam turns freely without rubbing either upright.

name: Smooth Releasehook
description: Drive the brace wedges home with short heavy mallet blows until the frame no longer shifts under a hand shove.

name: Measured Ballast
description: Throw the shoulder against the frame from each side and feel for any creak that tells of a loose joint.

name: Mild Tackle
description: Probe the soil beneath the sill with an iron rod to find soft places that would let the engine settle.

name: Steady Rigging
description: Hammer long stakes beside the sill so a hard release cannot walk the engine back across the ground.

name: Resting Longarm
description: Set the prop under the lifted beam arm and seat it firmly so the arm never falls on a working hand.

name: Deep Ballast
description: Circulate a little qi into the forearms before lifting so the shot sits lighter in the hands through many repeats.

name: Calm Slingpouch
description: Watch where the first shot lands and call the miss in paces so the crew can shift the weight or sling.

name: Measured Rigging
description: Read the dust and the dent of each landing to tell whether the throw fell short or ran long.

name: Fulcrum Note
description: Drive a peg at each trial landing and rope a range line back to the engine for later reference.

name: Tackleblow
description: Loosen or tighten the pin hook a hair after a trial shot so the sling frees earlier or later in the swing.

name: Swift Counterswing
description: Fire again with the corrected weight and release so the shot lands inside the pegged mark.

name: Tacklenote
description: Hold the breath and a thread of qi in the legs through the release so the crew does not flinch the pull.

name: Tacklegauge
description: Plait the sling cords from even strands and test each against a hung stone to prove it will not stretch unevenly.

name: Hangcradle Count
description: Match the two sling cords by laying them side by side and trimming the longer to the length of the shorter.

name: Warm Slingpouch
description: Swing a trial shot with a longer then a shorter sling to learn how length shifts the angle of departure.

name: Letgo Drop
description: Let the free cord ring slip off the pin at the top of the swing so the shot flies along the arm's last line.

name: Armgauge
description: Mark the worn spots on each sling after a day's firing and cut out any cord that has begun to fray.

name: Pullrope Review
description: Drop the pawl into the ratchet after each turn of the windlass so a slipped hand cannot let the beam fall.

name: Tacklereview
description: Guide the cable onto the drum in tight even layers so it does not bunch and bind under load.

name: Releasehook Gauge
description: Warm the palms with circulating qi and keep a steady crank turn through a long winding without cramping.

name: Deep Tackle
description: Two crewmen turn the handspikes in opposing rhythm so the windlass never stops between their pushes.

name: Tending Fulcrum
description: Listen to the cable and drum for the dry groan that warns of a fraying strand before the strain parts it.

name: Measured Pullrope
description: Back off the pawl one tooth at a time to lower the beam arm slowly onto its rest after a misfire.

name: Shortarm Note
description: Assign each crewman a station by name at the engine so every duty has one owner and no gap.

name: Ballast Review
description: Answer each loading call aloud in turn so the captain knows the sling the pouch and the shot are ready.

name: Releasehook Count
description: Raise a flat hand or a cloth when the engine is clear so the release is never ordered over a crewman.

name: Rigging Review
description: Chant the winding pace in low steady syllables that the whole team can match without breaking breath.

name: Smooth Tackle
description: Stop every motion at the halt call and hold the stance until the captain lifts the order.

name: Straight Swing
description: Give the release order in one hard syllable and pull the lanyard on its echo with the crew clear.

name: Slingpouch Review
description: Throw the voice from the belly with a little qi so orders carry across the noise of a firing line.

name: Skipping Heaveoff
description: After the throw the crew runs back to its stations in file and starts the next winding without a word.

name: Kind Hangcradle
description: Clear stones and loose gear from the engine yard so no crewman trips under the swing of the beam.

name: Smooth Longarm
description: Mark the beam's danger arc on the earth with a chalked cord so every newcomer knows where not to stand.

name: Releasehook Note
description: Note which side a snapped sling would throw its shot and keep the crew off that flank.

name: Heaveoff Trot
description: Slide out of the path of a slipped shot with a short quick step and a low guard.

name: Raised Shortarm
description: Raise an arm and a thread of qi over the head against falling splinters when a cable parts overhead.

name: Even Pullrope
description: Drag a fallen crewman out of the arc by the belt with a low steady pull before the next shot is loosed.
